name: Macedonian Glasoechko male diaphonic
lineage: Macedonian Glasoechko male two-voice diaphonic singing tradition of the Dolni Polog and Drimkol-Golo Brdo regions of western North Macedonia. The form features two-voice male singing in characteristic parallel-second and minor-third intervals over a sustained drone-tone (often an organ-point sustained by the second voice while the lead voice elaborates the melodic content), with most phrases cadencing on a unison-or-octave close. Distinguished from neighboring Balkan two-voice traditions by Glasoechko's Mijak-and-Šop dialect-specific cadential vocabulary and the characteristic Macedonian-pastoral functional context. The melodic vocabulary draws on regional pastoral-and-shepherd-call modal frameworks with characteristic narrow-range melodic-contour conventions. Accompanying instrumental contexts sometimes include the kaval end-blown shepherd-flute and the gajda Balkan bagpipe with double-reed chanter and drone-pipe. Performance traditionally outdoors in mountain-pasture contexts during summer transhumance, with the long-distance acoustic projection of the two-voice configuration suited to mountain-valley environments. The mid-twentieth-century rural depopulation of the Polog and Drimkol regions reduced active practitioners. Distinguished from Croatian Istrian diaphonic by Macedonian Glasoechko's drone-and-melody (vs Istrian's strict-two-voice-parallel) configuration and Macedonian-pastoral functional context; distinguished from Albanian iso-polyphony by Glasoechko's two-voice (vs Albanian three-or-four-voice) configuration; distinguished from neighboring Bulgarian male diaphonic by Macedonian-Mijak-dialect-specific cadential conventions.
